prices.question: How can I find fuel prices at a station?
prices.answer: Choose a city and fuel in the abastevo app. For each available price, the app shows whether it came from a community report or the ANP survey, when it was recorded and the reported price conditions.

survey.question: What is the ANP price survey?
survey.answer: Brazil’s National Agency of Petroleum, Natural Gas and Biofuels (ANP) publishes a weekly fuel price survey. It provides a historical reference for a sample in the survey week. The price currently shown at the pump may differ.

separate.question: How do community reports differ from ANP prices?
separate.answer: Drivers and others report prices they recently saw at a specific station. ANP provides an official recurring statistical survey. Abastevo displays the two sources separately and always identifies the source.

free.question: Will the app be free?
free.answer: Yes. Looking up prices and participating in the community are free. Any future paid features or services will never give a reported price extra weight or credibility.

precos.name: Prices and taxes
precos.description: How fuel prices take shape in Brazil: refinery costs, federal taxes, ICMS per liter, required blends, freight and margins, with official sources.
precos.intro: Why a liter costs what it does, how much of the price is tax and why the same fuel can cost different amounts in different cities.

escolher-combustivel.name: Choosing fuel
escolher-combustivel.description: Compare ethanol and gasoline, regular gasoline and additive grades, S10 and S500 diesel, and CNG to choose fuel for your vehicle and budget.
escolher-combustivel.intro: Compare fuels using official specifications, then do the math for your own vehicle.

economia.name: Fuel economy
economia.description: Practical ways to use less fuel, measure your car’s fuel economy from one full tank to the next and turn consumption into a cost per kilometer.
economia.intro: Build habits that reduce fuel use, measure your car’s consumption and work out what you spend per kilometer.

direitos-e-qualidade.name: Rights and quality
direitos-e-qualidade.description: Know your rights at Brazilian fuel stations, spot signs of adulterated fuel or a pump that delivers too little, and learn where to report problems.
direitos-e-qualidade.intro: Find out what the law guarantees when you refuel, how to check fuel quality and quantity, and whom to contact if something goes wrong.

dados.name: Data and transparency
dados.description: Understand the Brazilian ANP weekly survey and read fuel prices with their source, date and payment terms. See how official and community data differ.
dados.intro: See where the numbers on abastevo come from and what those numbers can tell you.

chrome.editorial: Text by the {team}. This English version was translated and reviewed with AI against the Portuguese original, which prevails. See the {policy} and how to request a correction.
chrome.guidesExplain: The guides explain the reasoning; the {tools} do the math with your numbers, no sign-up.
chrome.howGuidesBody: The guides are written in Portuguese by the {team}, cite the official source of every fact and show the last review date. The English versions are translated and reviewed with AI. Quoted prices are always examples; for real values, check the {prices} with their collection date. Full rules in the {policy}.
chrome.categoryFooter: See all {guides}, use the {tools} or check the {prices}.
chrome.howCalculatorsBody: Every page shows the formula and a worked example step by step, so you can check the math by hand, even with JavaScript off. The interactive version calculates in your browser: the values you type are never sent, stored or linked to you.
chrome.estimates: Results are estimates. Real consumption changes with traffic, load, terrain, tire pressure and driving style, and the price changes from station to station and week to week.
chrome.wherePrices: Where to get prices for the math
chrome.wherePricesBody: Use the price you saw at the pump or check the {prices}, always with the collection date. Learn what those numbers mean in the {methodology}.
chrome.pricesAnpLabel: ANP reference prices by state and city
chrome.toolFallback: The interactive calculator needs JavaScript. Without it, the math is still simple: follow the formula and the worked example below.
chrome.toolPrivacy: The math runs in your browser. Nothing you type is sent or stored.
chrome.toolPricesBody: Use the price you saw at the pump or check the {prices}, with the collection date. A reference price is a sample from the surveyed week, not a guarantee of today's price at the station.
chrome.browserRequirements: The interactive calculation uses JavaScript; the formula and the example work without it.
chrome.guidesHubIntro: Short, checkable texts on how prices are formed, how to choose fuel, how to spend less and what to do when something goes wrong at the station.
chrome.toolsHubIntro: Five simple calculators, each with its formula and a worked example. The math runs in your browser: nothing is sent, stored or tracked.
chrome.githubLabel: View on GitHub — Code with visible attribution
chrome.footerTagline: An open, independent project, not affiliated with ANP or any government. Community prices and the weekly ANP reference stay separate, always with source and date.
